question: Which species of sponges is commonly called glass sponge due to the presence of silica spicules?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Euplectella**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Euplectella** is commonly known as the glass sponge due to its silica spicules.
 
• Glass sponges are known for their intricate skeletons made of silica, which resemble glass.
 
• These sponges are primarily found in deep ocean waters and are known for their unique structural beauty.
 
• The silica spicules provide both support and protection to the sponge, making them distinct from other sponge species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sponges** are simple multicellular organisms that belong to the phylum Porifera.
 
• They have a porous body and an internal skeleton made of spicules or spongin fibers.
 
• Sponges are primarily marine organisms, though some species can be found in freshwater.
 
• They play a crucial role in marine ecosystems, including filtering water and providing habitat for other marine species.
 
• Sponges reproduce both sexually and asexually, and they have remarkable regenerative abilities.
